COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPMS No.2375 of 2025
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Mohd. Safdar, Advocate for the petitioner.
2. Mr. Raunak Pant, Advocate holding brief of Mr.
Naresh Pant, Advocate for the respondent no.1.
3. The petitioner has filed the present writ petition for
seeking a direction to the learned District Judge, Haridwar
to decide and conclude the proceedings of Miscellaneous
Case No.63 of 2023, Shubham Walia vs. Rajkumar and
others within stipulated time.
4. It is contended by the learned counsel for the
petitioner that the petitioner's land along with others was
acquired by the respondent no.1-National Highway
Authority of India ("NHAI"). The award was made and the
respondent no.1-NHAI was directed to make the payment
of the amount to the petitioner and other land owners. In
between, some dispute arose in respect of the
apportionment of the award between the parties, resulting
into filing of an application under Section 3H(4) of the
National Highways Act, 1956 in the court of District Judge,
Haridwar which was registered as Miscellaneous Case
No.63 of 2023, Shubham Walia vs. Rajkumar and others.
5. It is contended by the learned counsel for the
petitioner that the matter is being adjourned for one
reason and the other for the last two years while the
matter is extremely urgent and the petitioner are entitled
to get the speedy justice in accordance with the
Constitution of India which provides that the speedy

2
justice is a fundamental right of a citizen of this country.
6. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as
well as learned counsel for respondent no.1-NHAI and
perused the record of the case.
7. From perusal of the order-sheet, it transpires that
still all the respondents have not put in appearance in the
matter and their objections are yet not on record.
8. In such view of the matter, no case is made out at
this stage for any direction for expeditious disposal of the
Miscellaneous Case No.63 of 2023, Shubham Walia vs.
Rajkumar and others. Accordingly, the writ petition is
dismissed. However, liberty is given to the petitioner to
move this Court only when the pleadings between the
parties are exchanged.
